runner attaches it as `kwargs["capabilities"] = web_caps` and forwards `**kwargs` to the real Agent at runner.py:431 (text) and via `_pai_structured` at runner.py:619/637 (structured)

evidence: `web=agentic and any(bool(c.get("web")) for c in chunk)` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:333)
the capability is attached at the Agent/request level, not per-criterion (runner.py:348-352)
advisory.finding: The routing seam sets `web=True` for the whole request when ANY criterion in a co-chunked AGENT batch declares web, attaching the server-side web tool to criteria that did not opt in.
scenarios: A future routing change co-chunks T1 with another AGENT criterion that does not declare web

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a pass1_chunk test with a mixed agentic chunk (T1 + a non-web criterion) asserting req.web is True, and a chunk of only non-web criteria asserting False, to lock the `any()` aggregation.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:333: `web=agentic and any(bool(c.get("web")) for c in chunk)`
ABSENCE: no test constructs a chunk containing BOTH T1 and a non-web criterion in agentic mode to assert web is True (the `any` contract)
advisory.finding: The mixed-chunk web-flag threading in pass1_chunk (`web=agentic and any(bool(c.get('web')) for c in chunk)`) is untested: every test case uses a single-criterion chunk, so the `any()` aggregation over a chunk that mixes T1 with a non-web criterion is never exercised. A regression to `all(...)` or `chunk[0].get('web')` would keep all current tests green while silently dropping web grounding whenever T1 is co-chunked with another criterion (registry.chunk_by_facet can co-locate criteria in one chunk).
scenarios: T1 co-chunked with another agent-tier criterion by chunk_by_facet — web grounding silently dropped if the aggregation regresses to all()/first-element
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case: `passes.pass1_chunk(r, cfg, plan='a plan', chunk=[crits['T1'], crits['G1G2']], agentic=True); assert r.reqs[-1].web is True` and a two-non-web-criterion chunk asserting `web is False`.

evidence: `from pydantic_ai.capabilities import WebSearch` (new import added in _anthropic_web_search_capabilities)
Commit message: 'the supported successor of the deprecated builtin_tools='
Diff touches 7 files, none of which is a dependency manifest (pyproject.toml / requirements / uv.lock / poetry.lock) to pin the minimum pydantic-ai version exposing `pydantic_ai.capabilities`.
advisory.finding: The change depends on the new `pydantic_ai.capabilities.WebSearch` API (described as the successor of the deprecated `builtin_tools`) but no dependency manifest/lockfile change bumps or pins a minimum pydantic-ai version that exposes this module; an older pinned pydantic-ai would import-fail only on the flagged anthropic path at runtime.
scenarios: Environment resolves an older pydantic-ai without `pydantic_ai.capabilities.WebSearch`; the lazy import raises ImportError only when a flagged anthropic T1 request runs in production.

dropped.finding: The new test guards only on `pytest.importorskip("pydantic_ai")` (package presence) and does not assert that `pydantic_ai.capabilities.WebSearch` is importable/available, so CI can pass against a pydantic-ai version too old to provide the newly-required capability API.
scenarios: CI runs with a pinned older pydantic-ai lacking `capabilities`; the importorskip does not skip the module, but the capability-version assumption is never validated as a dependency contract.
